introduction: Explore how economic inequality can be measured and how it is impacted by different governmental pol

vocabulary.definition: the unfair situation in society when some people have more opportunities, money, etc. than other people
vocabulary.example: Income and wealth inequality are significant issues in many countries.
Is inequality inevitable in all societies?

vocabulary.definition: to be successful or fortunate, especially in financial respects; thrive
vocabulary.example: The company began to prosper after implementing new strategies.

vocabulary.definition: an example that opposes or contradicts an idea or theory
vocabulary.example: Despite common beliefs, there are counter-examples of capitalist countries with decreasing inequality.

vocabulary.definition: gradually increasing in extent or scope; moving forward
vocabulary.example: Progressive taxation systems aim to reduce income inequality by taxing higher incomes at a higher rate.

vocabulary.definition: the practice of passing on property, titles, debts, rights, and obligations upon the death of an individual
vocabulary.example: Inheritance taxes aim to limit the concentration of wealth within a few families over generations.
